children.translated_text: The goddess said:
O god of gods, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, compassionate great lord,

children.text: yoginām kiṃ sadā sevyam kaulānāṃ varapuṣṭidam ||
children.translated_text: what should always be practiced by yogins, and what gives excellent nourishment to Kaulas?
What removes the restlessness of the mind, and what grants the fruit of <s>samādhi</s>?

children.text: vadasva tad aśeṣeṇa yady ahaṃ tava vallabhā ||
children.translated_text: Tell that to me completely, if I am dear to you.
<s>Śiva</s> said:
This is not to be spoken, O beautiful-limbed one, even among gods, asuras, and men.

children.text: kathayāmi tava prītyā guhyād guhyataram mahat ||
children.translated_text: Yet out of love for you I shall tell the great secret, more secret than the secret.
Having heard it, you too must guard it carefully amid the peril posed by the paśus.

children.text: valo nāma mahān āsīd asuro balavān purā ||
children.translated_text: Long ago there was a great asura named <s>Vala</s>, mighty in strength.

children.text: jitvā suragaṇān sarvān indro 'bhūt svayam eva saḥ
children.translated_text: After conquering all the hosts of gods, he himself became <s>Indra</s>.
Then all the dwellers in heaven fled, disturbed by fear.
Placing <s>Puraṃdara</s> at their head, they conferred and reached a firm decision:
'There is no other help for us against him than the glorious <s>Madhusūdana</s>.'

children.text: iti saṃcintya te sarve prayayuḥ parameśvaram
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, they all went to the supreme lord,
who was being praised by sages and attended by siddhas and kiṃnaras.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇḍarikākṣaṃ praṇamya daṇḍavad bhuvi
children.translated_text: Seeing that lotus-eyed one, they bowed down like staffs upon the earth,
and these gods, led by <s>Śakra</s>, spoke with joined palms:
'Homage to you, <s>Hari</s>, remover of every sorrow,
and homage again and again to the lord of all, who destroys the affliction of the gods.
Homage to you, the three-formed one, who brings about creation, continuance, and dissolution,
who is beyond the guṇas, pure, and higher even than the highest.
Homage to you, the self of all, endowed with every power;
homage again and again to you, the omniscient witness of all worlds.

children.text: iti stutvā ca sakalam tad vṛttāntam nyavedayan
children.translated_text: After praising him thus, they reported the whole course of events.

children.text: śaraṇam tvām gatāḥ sarve trāhi naś caiva nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'We have all come to you for refuge; protect us always.

children.text: durācāro valo mṛtyum yathā yāty acireṇa saḥ
children.translated_text: You should so act that the wicked <s>Vala</s> soon meets death,

children.text: rakṣāsmākaṃ ca śakrasya tathā kartuṃ tvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: and that protection be granted to us and to <s>Śakra</s>.'

children.text: śrutvedam vacanam teṣām idam āha puraṃdaram
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of theirs, he said this to <s>Puraṃdara</s>:
'I know this affair of that evil-souled <s>Vala</s>.

children.text: brahmaṇā na mayā vāpi na sa vadhyaḥ śivena vā
children.translated_text: He is not to be slain by <s>Brahmā</s>, nor by me, nor by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tvayaiva vadhyo bhavitā sa durātmā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He will be slain by you alone, that evil-souled one; there is no doubt.
Report all this to <s>Maheśa</s>, O <s>Puraṃdara</s>.

children.text: sa eva bhagavān sarvam etaj jānāti śaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: That blessed <s>Śaṃkara</s> alone knows all this.
He will arrange everything you desire; go.
And by your effort propitiate him, for he is affectionate to his good devotees.'

children.text: atha praṇamya śakras tam samāyāto mamāntikam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, having bowed to him, came to my presence.
Coming there with a pure disposition, he bowed and stood with joined palms.
With various hymns, spoken in a voice choked by devotion, he praised me,
the lord dwelling on <s>Kailāsa</s>, withdrawn in meditation.
Through many recitations of hymns, resounding from that praise,
all that knowledge, great and complete, arose on every side.

children.text: asyaiva vadhyaḥ sa valo durātmāsau bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Knowing that in the future that evil-souled <s>Vala</s> would be slain by this very one,

children.text: bhaviṣyam etad vijñāya śakram āhūya saṃnidhim ||
children.translated_text: and discerning what was to come, I summoned <s>Śakra</s> near.

children.text: tasmai tat paramaṃ jñānam dattvāvocam idaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having given him that supreme knowledge, I spoke these words:
'This is the knowledge called <s>Trailokyavijayā</s>, hard to obtain in the three worlds.
There is no knowledge greater than the knowledge of <s>Trailokyavijayā</s>, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
It removes all dullness and reveals the supreme self.
It is the abode of unbroken bliss, non-dual, the highest state.
It steadies the mind and destroys disease, grief, and burning distress.
It gives strength and nourishment and completely brings about the highest perfection of yoga.

children.text: niṣevyatām iyaṃ saṃvit sthīyatām ca mamāntike ||
children.translated_text: Let this <s>saṃvit</s> (awareness-substance) be practiced, and remain near me.

children.text: tato gatvā vatsarānte sa valo jeṣyate tvayā
children.translated_text: Then, when a year has passed, that <s>Vala</s> will be conquered by you.'

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ sa mayā prāñjaliś cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by me, he stood with joined palms and said this:
<s>Śakra</s> said:
O god of gods, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, omniscient knower of all principles,

children.text: vidhinā kena sevyeyaṃ ko vā mantro viśodhane ||
children.translated_text: by what procedure should this be practiced, and what is the mantra for purification?

children.text: tarpaṇe svīkṛtau mantraḥ saṃvidaḥ kṛpayā vibho
children.translated_text: What is the mantra for offering and for accepting <s>saṃvit</s>, gracious lord?

children.text: sarvam etad aśeṣeṇa sāṅgopāṅgam vadasva me ||
children.translated_text: Tell me all this completely, together with its limbs and subsidiary limbs.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu śakra mahābhāga sarvam etad vadāmi te
children.translated_text: Listen, greatly fortunate <s>Śakra</s>; I shall tell you all this.

children.text: śrutvā gopaya yatnena tad evācara nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard it, guard it carefully, and practice just that always.
First I shall tell in order the names of her called <s>Trailokyavijayā</s>,
which are everywhere exceedingly secret, out of affection for you.
<s>Trailokyavijayā</s>, perfected, giver of siddhi, root of siddhi,

children.text: jñānam saṃvit saṃvidā ca śyāmā bhaṅgā rasāyanā ||
children.translated_text: knowledge, <s>saṃvit</s>, <s>Saṃvidā</s>, dark one, <s>Bhaṅgā</s>, elixir,
giver of yoga, served by yogins, illuminator of the path of yoga,
<s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, born from <s>Brahman</s>, giver of the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>,
deity of speech, subduer, victorious one, giver of victory,
giver of excellent <s>samādhi</s>, and destroyer of ignorance: these are the twenty-one names.
Because of the distinction of white, red, yellow, and black flowers, she is fourfold.
The white-flowered one is <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>; the red-flowered one is kṣatriya.

children.text: pītapuṣpā tu vaiśyā ca śūdrā tu kṛṣṇapuṣpikā
children.translated_text: The yellow-flowered one is vaiśya, and the black-flowered one is śūdra.
Carefully drawing forth the leaves of these, together with their seeds,
roasted in ghee and powdered on a stone slab,
one should take <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, horn, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, coriander, and rock salt,
<s>śaṭī</s>, <s>tālīśapatra</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, and <s>nāgakesara</s>,

children.text: yamānīdvayam methī ca jīrakadvayam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the two kinds of <s>yamānī</s>, fenugreek, and the two kinds of cumin as well.
These, in equal parts, dried in the sun, he should powder.

children.text: gṛhītvā cūrṇam etat tu saṃviccūrṇaṃ tu tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: Taking this powder, one should add an equal quantity of the powder of <s>saṃvit</s>.

children.text: ubhayos tu samam kṛtvā sitāṃ saṃmiśrayed ghṛte
children.translated_text: Having made the two equal, one should mix the white substance with ghee.

children.text: miśrayitvā caturthāṃśam samaṃ madhu ghṛtam tathā ||
children.translated_text: After mixing, one should add a fourth part, and likewise an equal amount of honey and ghee.

children.text: punaḥ śilātale piṣṭvā triṣu gandham pravartayet
children.translated_text: Again, after grinding it on a stone slab, one should set the fragrance in motion in the three.
Having placed it in front in a vessel of gold or the like, then, in sequence,
one should perform its purification with four mantras.
Placing the tips of the hands there, one should purify it according to rule.
<s>Oṃ</s>, O <s>Saṃvid</s>, born of <s>Brahman</s>, daughter of <s>Brahman</s>, ever stainless,

children.text: bhairavāṇām ca tṛptyarthaṃ pavitrā bhava sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: for the satisfaction of the <s>Bhairavas</s> too, be pure always.

children.text: oṃ brāhmaṇyai namaḥ svāhā brahmāṇīśodhane manuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, svāhā: this is the mantra for purifying the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>.
<s>Oṃ</s>, O goddess, whose action is rooted in siddhi, awakener of those of deficient understanding,
subduer of king and subjects, trident in the throat of enemies,

children.text: oṃ kṣatriyāyai namaḥ svāhā śodhayed aparāṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, svāhā: then one should purify the next one.
<s>Oṃ</s>, O blazing fire for the fuel of ignorance, O fire of knowledge, whose form is knowledge,

children.text: ānandaś cāhutim prītiṃ samyagjñānam prayaccha me ||
children.translated_text: grant me bliss, oblation, affection, and perfect knowledge.

children.text: dṛīm vaiśyāyai nama.ḥ svāhā vaiśyāṃ saṃśodhayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dṛīm</s>, homage to the <s>Vaiśyā</s>, svāhā: then one should purify the <s>Vaiśyā</s>.
<s>Oṃ</s>, I bow, I bow, O revealer of the path of yoga,
O mother, conqueror of the three worlds, become the giver of the fruit of samādhi.

children.text: kṛīm śūdrāyai namaḥ svāhā śūdrāyāḥ śodhanaṃ manuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛīm</s>, homage to the <s>Śūdrā</s>, svāhā: this is the mantra for the purification of the <s>Śūdrā</s>.
<s>Oṃ</s>, O immortal one, born of immortality, pourer of immortality,
draw in, draw in the nectar; give siddhi.
Bring such-and-such a person under my control, svāhā.

children.text: dvidhānto 'yaṃ manuḥ proktaś catuṣkāṇām ca śodhane ||
children.translated_text: This mantra ending in the twofold way is taught for the purification of the four.
One should mantra-empower <s>Ānandabhairava</s> and <s>Ānandabhairavī</s> with the tattva.
<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Soma</s> are to end with the mother-syllables.
Joined with the left-hand syllable <s>ka</s> and joined with wind and the half-moon,
one should then utter the crest-mantra, saying, 'to <s>Ānandabhairava</s>'.
This is the mantra of <s>Ānandabhairava</s>; the mantra of <s>Ānandabhairavī</s>

children.text: pūrvavad bījam ālikhya candraṃ hitvā dinaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: is made by writing the seed-syllable as before, omitting the moon, and bringing in the day.

children.text: kaṃe vamākṣi saṃyojya sudhadevyai manur dviśaḥ
children.translated_text: Joining <s>kaṃ</s> with the left eye, the mantra for <s>Sudhādevī</s> is said twice.
One should place the root mantra over it seven times.
Then the mudrā beginning with invocation, and after that the cow and womb mudrās,
the binding of the directions, preceded by three claps with finger-snaps.
Then, with divine sight and with heel-strikes, one should strike down the obstacles.

children.text: saptadhā tarpayed brahmarandhre mulaṃ japen manum ||
children.translated_text: One should satisfy it seven times and recite the root mantra in the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>.
In the thousand-petalled lotus, in the guru-lotus, one should make offering with the sign-mudrā.

children.text: tridhā vā tarpayed bhaktyā sakṛd vāpi nijecchayā ||
children.translated_text: Or one may make offering three times with devotion, or even once, according to one's own wish.
There one should satisfy the guru called supreme, and then the higher-and-lower guru.
With the mantra, remembering that mantra, one should satisfy <s>Ānandabhairava</s> and <s>Ānandabhairavī</s>.
In the heart, with the root mantra and the tattva-mudrā, one should satisfy the goddess,
with <s>Saṃvid</s>, three times or once, in a measure equal to sesame or mung bean.
<s>Aiṃ</s>, speak, speak, O <s>Vāgvādinī</s>,
be steady at the tip of my tongue.
After saying, 'maker of all beings subject to control, svāhā,' one should offer into the mouth.
Then with the divine nectar of the mouth one should receive the <s>Saṃvid</s>.
With milk, water, ghee, honey-wine, rock salt, or salt,
or with sugar, or with jaggery, or with mud, or with banana,

children.text: yad yad vā madhuraṃ dravyam paṅkāmrapanasādikam
children.translated_text: or whatever sweet substance there may be, such as mango and jackfruit pulp,
with all of that, <s>Vijayā</s> should be received by practitioners of poetic accomplishment.
<s>Vijayā</s>, when joined with milk, increases pure bliss;
she produces great brilliance and removes defects of the eye and the like.
She, again, when joined with water, destroys all living beings' decay.
With ghee she establishes intelligence; as the goddess of speech she brings mastery.
She establishes excellent inspiration and an exceedingly pure intellect.

children.text: kaphadoṣān aśeṣāmś ca madhunā saha nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: Together with honey she destroys all disorders of phlegm without remainder.
With rock salt and with salt she gives a great digestive fire.
With sugar or with jaggery she destroys colic, acidity, and bile.
She calms diarrhea and crushes asthma and cough.
She removes grahaṇī disease arising from āmavāta.
Joined with all sweet things, she destroys every illness.
She gives strength and nourishment, and bestows a sweet voice.
She reveals knowledge, discriminating knowledge, skill, character, and the path.
What need is there to say much here? She is the very form of pure consciousness.
Out of affection for you I have revealed what is well hidden in all the āgamas.

children.text: atha svīkṛtya vijayām sahasrāre guruṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having received <s>Vijayā</s>, one should worship the guru in the thousand-petalled lotus.
Having uttered the pādukā-mantra, one should present it with the fourth-case ending.
With the seed-syllable whose nature is the five elements, one should offer the five beginning with fragrance.
Having recited the glorious guru's sandals, one should bow down on the ground like a staff.

children.text: iṣṭadevaṃ ca tanmantram prajapan viharet kṛtī ||
children.translated_text: Then, reciting one's chosen deity and that deity's mantra, the accomplished practitioner should move about.

children.text: evam abhyāsataḥ śakraḥ pratyahaṃ vatsaraṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: By practicing in this way every day for a year, O <s>Śakra</s>,
you will become radiant, strong, eloquent, intelligent, and lovely to behold.
Endowed with beauty and youth, and possessed of many virtues,
you will become so, without doubt, through the use of this substance.

children.text: saṃvidaḥ kevalāyās tu sevanāt kiṃ na sidhyati
children.translated_text: Through the use of <s>Saṃvid</s> alone, what does not become accomplished?
Between <s>Saṃvid</s> and liquor, <s>Saṃvid</s> alone is superior.
Therefore the rite of <s>Saṃvid</s> should be performed by the best practitioners.
Once a day, twice a day, three times a day, or five times a day,

children.text: tolakam vā tadardhaṃ vā tolakadvayam eva vā
children.translated_text: whether a tolaka, half of that, or two tolakas,

children.text: na hi nyūnādhikā mātrā yathā bhavati nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the measure should not be deficient or excessive, as is always proper.
When the measure is deficient or excessive, the true fruit does not arise.

children.text: tasmāt pramāṇamātrā hi kartavyā siddhim icchatā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who desires siddhi should observe only the proper measure.

children.text: etat te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ vijayākalpam uttamam
children.translated_text: This entire supreme rite of victory has been told to you.

children.text: prasādād acirād asyā vānchitam te bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: By her grace, what you desire will soon come to pass.

children.text: ity uktaḥ sa mayā śakro nirbhayānandananditaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Śakra</s> was thus addressed by me, he rejoiced in fearless bliss.

children.text: bhaktyā paramayā yuktas tat kavtum upacakrame ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with supreme devotion, he began to perform that rite.
For a year, every day, carefully, at the three times of day,
<s>Śakra</s>, disciplined, worshipped <s>Vijayā</s> according to the rule,
and, after conquering <s>Balāsura</s>, he then became king of the gods.
Having obtained the abode of the subduer, he gained his desire.
This has been spoken as a secret, supremely concealed teaching.
It must never be told anywhere at any time.
Yet because of your longing, I have indeed told you this former event.
O goddess, this too should be carried out by you according to the rule.
Thus, in the Cīnatantra, the seventh chapter.
